idea.body: Multiplying a multi-digit number works by splitting it into place-value parts, multiplying each part, then adding the results. 34 times 6 splits into 30 plus 4: 6 times 30 is 180, 6 times 4 is 24, and 180 plus 24 is 204. This is what the standard algorithm's carrying does in shorthand. It is also the area model: a rectangle split into smaller pieces, each piece's area found separately, then every piece added for the whole rectangle.

workedExample.prompt: A print shop runs 46 posters in each of 7 batches. How many posters is that?
steps: Split 46 into 40 plus 6.
7 times 40 is 280.
7 times 6 is 42.
280 plus 42 is 322.
The shop prints 322 posters.

figure.alt: An area model splitting 46 by 7 into two labelled boxes: 40 by 7 worth 280, and 6 by 7 worth 42.

ways.name: Split one number
ways.when: Use this for any multi-digit times single-digit multiplication.
steps: Split 46 into 40 plus 6.
Multiply each part by 7: 7 times 40 is 280.
7 times 6 is 42.
Add the parts: 280 plus 42 is 322.
ways.trap: Adding the parts before finishing both multiplications.

figure.alt: An area model splitting 46 by 7 into two labelled boxes: 40 by 7 worth 280, and 6 by 7 worth 42, totalling 322.

ways.name: Column method
ways.when: Use this when you want one written line per number, with carrying.
steps: Write 34 above 6, lined up on the right.
Multiply the ones digit: 6 times 4 is 24, write 4, carry 2.
Multiply the tens digit: 6 times 3 is 18, plus the carried 2 is 20.
Write the 20 next to the 4: the product is 204.
ways.trap: Forgetting to add the carried digit before writing the final digits.

ways.name: Doubling and halving
ways.when: Use this when one factor halves evenly and the other doubles into a round number.
steps: Halve the first number and double the second: 16 becomes 8, 25 becomes 50.
The product stays the same: 8 times 50.
Halve again and double again: 8 becomes 4, 50 becomes 100.
4 times 100 is 400.
ways.trap: Halving one number without doubling the other, which changes the product.

ways.name: Round and adjust
ways.when: Use this when one factor sits one away from a round number.
steps: Round 19 up to 20, an easier number.
Multiply the rounded number: 20 times 7 is 140.
19 is 1 less than 20, so one extra group of 7 got counted.
Subtract that extra group: 140 minus 7 is 133.
ways.trap: Forgetting to subtract the extra group after rounding up.

stretch.prompt: Which expression is equal to 24 times 15?
explanation: 24 splits into 20 plus 4 by place value.
Multiplying that whole split by 15 matches (20 + 4) x 15.
The other choices multiply only part of the split, or group the numbers incorrectly.
stretch.useAgain: when you need to recognise the correct place-value split behind a multiplication.
hints: Split the multi-digit number by place value first.
Multiply the whole split by the other factor, not just one part of it.
stretch.socraticHint: Does multiplying only one part of a split number by the other factor still give the full product?
